FAQ ['What happens if the AI agent can’t help?', 'It never pretends to be human and never asks for card numbers, passwords or one-time codes. When a caller wants a person, the agent transfers the call to the number you set — or, if you haven’t set one, offers to take a message with a name, callback number and the message, which lands in your inbox. On a keypad menu, callers can always reach voicemail. Anyone who asks not to be called again is removed from the list and the call ends politely.']
FAQ ['Which countries need an ID check and how long does it take?', 'United States, Canada, Puerto Rico and Colombia numbers go live in about a minute. United Kingdom, Netherlands, Israel, New Zealand, Australia, Ireland, Hong Kong, Czech Republic, Estonia, Mexico, Romania, Slovakia and South Africa ask for contact details, an address and sometimes an ID before the number activates — telecom regulation, not us. You pay first and the number is held for you while you fill in the details (about 2 minutes); the carrier then reviews them, usually within a few hours and up to 3 business days. Your plan starts when the number is active, and you get a full refund if it isn’t approved.']
FAQ ['Do you scrub numbers or enforce quiet hours?', 'Your do-not-call list is enforced on every campaign — Bulk IVR and AI agent, web and Telegram bot: numbers on it are never dialed and never billed. We don’t check public Do-Not-Call registries for you and we don’t enforce quiet hours automatically: you schedule each campaign, set a daily call limit and repeat it daily or weekly, and you’re responsible for calling only people who have agreed to hear from you, at reasonable hours where they live.']
